The new commits do two things: they add the empty-slice guard to `average` (which fixes the previously flagged divide-by-zero, `f-divide-by-zero`), and they add a new `first` function.

The new `first` function has a real problem. `last` at `src/lib.rs:3` clamps with `saturating_sub`, so an oversized `n` yields all the items — its doc even promises "or all of them when there are fewer." `first` makes no such accommodation: `&items[..n]` panics whenever `n > items.len()`. A caller who reasonably passes a large `n` (mirroring how `last` tolerates one) gets a panic instead. `&items[..n.min(items.len())]` matches the sibling function's contract; the doc comment should then say "or all of them when there are fewer." There are no tests anywhere in the crate, and a test calling `first(&[1], 5)` would have caught this.

Nothing else changed: the integer truncation in `average` is unchanged from the prior head, and that finding was dropped, so I'm not re-raising it.
